implemented.scope: src/fastedit/inference/chunked_merge.py (_check_hallucinations, _real_lines, _parse_snippet_hunks, _compute_expected_merged, _validator_replacement_key, plus removal of the obsolete _order_preserved); tests/test_hallucination_validation.py (extended regression matrix).
implemented.design: Replaced the global-multiset validator with an expected-output synthesizer that walks the snippet's marker-separated hunks and the original in parallel. Each hunk's non-marker lines are classified as context anchors (forward-scan matches) or new lines via a single forward scan; markers are PRESERVATION WILDCARDS that delimit hunks but carry no payload. The expected merged is built section by section: a leading-new section replaces every original before the first anchor, in-between sections replace the first min(N_new, |gap|) originals and preserve the rest, and the trailing section follows the same pattern with marker/no-marker semantics controlling preservation of the remainder. The new lines are emitted in snippet order so a multiset-equivalent but order-corrupt merge (counterexample 4) is rejected. An independent replacement-key cross-check (assignment LHS, declaration name, flow-statement kind) rejects ambiguous pairings where a single snippet key matches multiple originals in the local gap. Marker leakage is caught by a raw-line scan of the merged chunk before any structural comparison. The full expected sequence is compared directly to the merged list, so missing required code, invented lines, unrelated deletions, reordering, and unsupported duplication are caught by one check.
implemented.why_this_design: The fix-round-1 forward-scan implementation lost two properties: (a) markers were stripped before the comparison so the marker region semantics were invisible, treating every unmentioned original line as replaceable; and (b) the order check ran only on the snippet's preserved-line list, missing reorders of snippet-declared new lines. The new algorithm reconstructs the expected merged output declaratively — markers mean 'preserve this region', leading new lines mean 'replace the gap before the first anchor', in-between new lines mean 'replace the first N and preserve the rest', and the cross-check makes pairings provable. The expected sequence is a single deterministic list, so the validation step is a direct equality check that subsumes every property the contract requires.

remaining: Nothing in scope. All four coordinator counterexamples produce the expected outcome (1.0/0.0 as required) and every regression in the original VAL-001 matrix still passes. The validator's private signature and downstream call sites at chunked_merge.py:833 and 842 are unchanged, so the 0.85-retry / 0.5-reject threshold machinery continues to operate correctly.

The helper signature _check_hallucinations(original_chunk, merged_chunk, snippet) -> float is preserved verbatim, as required by the contract's backward-compatibility constraint.

corrections.issue: Validator treated every unmentioned original line as replaceable, losing marker-region preservation semantics.
corrections.resolution: Markers are now parsed as hunks delimiters; their bounded region is reconstructed from the surrounding context anchors and the marker itself contributes no payload. Lines behind a marker are preserved unless the snippet explicitly declares their replacement via in-section new lines (positional) or via a replacement key (declarative).

corrections.issue: Order check ran only on the snippet's preserved-line list, missing reorders of snippet-declared new lines.
corrections.resolution: The expected-output synthesizer emits new lines in snippet order at their declared local positions; the final direct list comparison catches any reorder. test_corrupt_new_line_reorder_rejected (was 1.0, now 0.0) and test_new_line_reorder_within_preserved_block_rejected (was 1.0, now 0.0) confirm.

corrections.issue: Cardinality shortcuts (the issue proposal len(lost_anchors) <= len(snippet_new)) accept additive edits that drop unrelated lines and duplicate output.
corrections.resolution: Each in-section new line is bound to a specific original position by either (a) positional pairing with the first min(N_new, |gap|) originals in the local gap or (b) a replacement-key match. Unrelated deletions, duplicates, and reorderings all produce an expected/merged mismatch and are rejected.

corrections.issue: worker_result / design_decision / minimalism_descent / tests / checks / out_of_bounds / interfaces_changed had wrong JSON shapes in REP-W-001.
corrections.resolution: REP-W-002 uses the contract-correct schema: worker_result is one of success|partial|blocked; design_decision is a boolean; minimalism_descent is a string; tests is an object with added array, command, exit_code, anti_gaming; checks is an array of objects with kind, command, exit_code, observed; out_of_bounds is an array; interfaces_changed is an array. All other required array-shaped fields are arrays.

discoveries.finding: Marker preservation requires per-section synthesis, not a global set diff. The previous global-multiset implementation could not distinguish 'the marker preserved this region' from 'this original was silently dropped'.
discoveries.impact: Closed the bystander-deletion bypass that scored a merge that dropped must_survive() as 1.0.

discoveries.finding: Snippet-new lines must be ordered relative to snippet position, not relative to the original. A multiset-equivalent reorder of new lines violates the snippet's declared structure even when no original is touched.
discoveries.impact: Closed the new-line reorder bypass that scored [A, Y, X, B] as 1.0 against snippet [A, X, Y, B].

discoveries.finding: Replacement-key matching requires a generic identity extractor (assignment LHS, declaration name, flow-statement kind). The existing _replacement_key in text_match.py only handles assignment LHS; the validator needs flow-statement and declaration identity too. Implemented as _validator_replacement_key to keep the change scoped to chunked_merge.py without touching text_match.py's API.

When the next hunk in a multi-hunk snippet has no context anchor (a pure-insertion hunk between two markers), the previous-hunk's trailing region must skip past it and look at the next-next hunk's first context anchor. Without this, the expected merged output incorrectly preserved originals between the two markers.

conventions.no_hardcoding: The validator is a pure function of (original_chunk, merged_chunk, snippet). No language-specific branches, no framework-specific heuristics, no per-call-site dispatch. Marker semantics, replacement identities, and section structure are derived generically from the snippet text.

After implementation, all 7 pass. None of the round-1 regression tests were weakened, deleted, or rewritten.
